column1: Add Binary — given two binary strings `a` and `b`, return their sum as a binary string. Example: '11', '1' → '100'; '1010', '1011' → '10101'.
column2: PATTERN: Manual digit addition with carry. | INSIGHT: Walk both from the END; sum bits + carry; build result reversed. | STEPS: 1) i=len(a)-1, j=len(b)-1, carry=0, ans=[]. 2) While i>=0 or j>=0 or carry: s=carry; if i>=0: s+=int(a[i]); i-=1; if j>=0: s+=int(b[j]); j-=1; ans.append(str(s%2)); carry=s//2. 3) Return ''.join(reversed(ans)). | TIME/SPACE: O(max(m,n)) / O(max(m,n)). | PITFALL: Loop while carry is true even after both strings exhausted — final 1 may carry.

PATTERN: Bit-by-bit shift OR. | INSIGHT: Loop 32 times: result = (result<<1) | (n & 1); n >>= 1. | STEPS: 1) ans=0. 2) For _ in range(32): ans=(ans<<1)|(n&1); n>>=1. 3) Return ans. | TIME/SPACE: O(32) / O(1). | PITFALL: Always exactly 32 iterations regardless of leading zeros.

column1: Number of 1 Bits — given uint32 n, return the number of '1' bits in its binary representation (Hamming weight). Example: 11 (0b1011) → 3; 128 (0b10000000) → 1.
column2: PATTERN: Brian Kernighan's trick. | INSIGHT: n & (n-1) clears the lowest set bit; count iterations until n becomes 0. | STEPS: 1) count=0. 2) While n: n &= n-1; count+=1. 3) Return count. | TIME/SPACE: O(set bits) / O(1). | PITFALL: Faster than checking each of 32 bits one-by-one.

column1: Single Number — every element appears TWICE except one; find the unique one in O(n) time and O(1) space. Example: [2,2,1] → 1; [4,1,2,1,2] → 4.
column2: PATTERN: XOR all elements. | INSIGHT: a XOR a = 0; a XOR 0 = a; XOR is commutative and associative — pairs cancel, leaving the unique value. | STEPS: 1) ans=0. 2) For x in nums: ans^=x. 3) Return ans. | TIME/SPACE: O(n) / O(1). | PITFALL: Only works because every other element appears EXACTLY twice.

column1: Single Number II — every element appears THREE times except one; find the unique one in O(n) and O(1). Example: [2,2,3,2] → 3; [0,1,0,1,0,1,99] → 99.
column2: PATTERN: Two-bit state machine (ones, twos). | INSIGHT: Track bits seen 1× and 2×; the third occurrence cancels both. After processing, `ones` holds the answer. | STEPS: 1) ones=twos=0. 2) For x in nums: ones=(ones^x) & ~twos; twos=(twos^x) & ~ones. 3) Return ones. | TIME/SPACE: O(n) / O(1). | PITFALL: Easier-to-derive alternative: for each of 32 bits, sum bit-counts mod 3.

column1: Bitwise AND of Numbers Range — return bitwise AND of all integers in [left, right] inclusive. Example: 5,7 → 4; 0,0 → 0; 1,2147483647 → 0.
column2: PATTERN: Find common high-bit prefix. | INSIGHT: AND of any range collapses to the common high-bit prefix of left and right; bits below that diverge across the range. | STEPS: 1) shift=0. 2) While left<right: left>>=1; right>>=1; shift+=1. 3) Return left<<shift. | TIME/SPACE: O(log n) / O(1). | PITFALL: Brute-force AND-loop is impossible for large ranges; the prefix observation is the key.
